meta.what: Who controls the tankers carrying Russia's seaborne crude and oil-product exports, by country of the beneficial owner / commercial controller (not flag, not front-company registration), 2021-2026, split into the mainstream fleet (G7+-linked: owned, managed, flagged or IG P&I-insured in a price-cap country, KSE 'white') and the shadow fleet; and the resulting gross freight revenue per country. Russian-owned and Russian-controlled tankers (Sovcomflot and its UAE/HK fronts, Russian managers, half of opaque Seychelles/Marshall Islands/unknown owners) are kept as a separate Russian pool and count for no foreign country.
meta.units: Shares: fraction of the segment's barrels (crude, products, or crude+products weighted 58/42). freight: EUR bn GROSS freight revenue (not profit), nominal, ECB yearly average USD/EUR (2021 1.1827, 2022 1.0530, 2023 1.0813, 2024 1.0824, 2025 1.1300, 2026 1.1629 = same as shipping.json); 2026 = Jan-Aug, not annualised. Each value {low, central, high}, ~90% range.
meta.method: 1) Mainstream vs shadow by segment: combined shadow share from KSE Shadow Fleet Tracker (Sep 2026; monthly Apr 2022-Aug 2026, read from chart geometry: 23% Apr-Dec 2022, 43% 2023, 63% 2024, 55% 2025, 58% Jan-Aug 2026; Jan-Mar 2022 ~7%; 2021 ~6% per Bloomberg/Brookings); products shadow share from KSE Russian Oil Tracker monthly statements (31-52% in 2023-24, 18-37% in 2025); crude = residual (23%, 49%, 79%, 76%, 78%). 2) Greek beneficial owners' share of each segment from Lloyd's List, S&P Global, Kpler, Windward and KSE top-10 tables (see GRC). 3) Rest of the mainstream segment split by educated fractions from the pre-war fleet structure and KSE top-10 tables (Turkey, Cyprus, Malta, Kuwait/AMPTC, Singapore, India, China, UAE; Russian owners still IG-insured in 2021-22). 4) Shadow segment split by KSE monthly shadow volumes by country of ship/commercial manager, then mapped to the beneficial controller: Russia-managed 100% Russian; UAE-managed foreign 15/20/25/32/20% (2022-26) else Russian (Sovcomflot chain, refine.json); KSE 'China' 55% mainland (80% foreign) / 45% Hong Kong (65% foreign); India 45-55% foreign; Singapore 80%; Seychelles, Marshall Islands and unknown managers 50% Russian, 50% spread over the hubs (ARE 37, HKG 21, CHN 16, IND 16, VNM 5, MYS 5); 'other' managers TUR 18, VNM 12, AZE 8, MYS 6, OMN 6, IDN 4, GEO 3, EGY 3, SAU 2, Russian fronts 25, opaque 13. 5) Freight = crude pool x crude share + products pool x products share (pools from shipping.json, 2026 crude pool 11.0 per refine.json freight_per_bbl), Chinese/HK shadow crude at 0.6x per barrel (Kozmino short haul), + LNG part unchanged from shipping.json. Ranges: share factor by certainty (B 0.8-1.25, C 0.55-1.7, D 0.35-2.4; Greece year-specific) combined with pool uncertainty as independent log errors.

how_to_use: Replaces the country allocation of FREIGHT in shipping.json (field countries.ISO3.freight and baseline_2019_2021 freight part). If the builder uses countries.ISO3.freight from this file: (a) do NOT also apply refine.json shipping_control freight_scale_vs_current_model (the Russian carve-out for UAE/IND/CHN/HKG is already inside these shares); (b) do NOT apply the 2026 freight x1.065 factor in apply_shipping (the 2026 crude pool here is already 11.0 instead of 9.7); (c) the insurance_finance items in shipping.json that follow owner shares can be scaled by freight_scale_vs_shipping_json; (d) ship_sales, registry and P&I-by-insurer parts of shipping.json are unchanged; (e) SYC, MHL get no freight here (fronts; their volume is split Russia/hubs), so the Seychelles 20% cut in fix_artefacts no longer matters for freight; (f) profit factors (SHIPPING_PROFIT freight 0.2/0.35/0.5) and overlap shares still apply on top - these are gross values. replacement_share_tables gives CRUDE and PRODUCTS share tables in the format of working/shipping/build.py (RUS = Russian own and controlled pool).

ARE.reasoning: Two parts. (1) Shadow: KSE shows UAE-registered managers handled 12-18% of all seaborne barrels in 2022-24, 10% in 2025, 7% in 2026, but most is the Sovcomflot chain (Sun Ship and SCF Mgmt, OFAC-identified as Sovcomflot-owned; then Stream, Fornax, Avebury, Nova, Dreamer, Greenlight, Albatross, Lynx, Grace, Twister operating ex-Sovcomflot tankers). Only 15-32% is treated as truly UAE-resident control (refine.json). (2) 37% of the opaque Seychelles/Marshall Islands/unknown remainder, and UAE companies in the mainstream products trade (e.g. Onex DMCC in KSE product tables). Certainty C.

CHN.reasoning: KSE 'China' managers (incl. Hong Kong; 55% mainland assumed) rose from 2% of seaborne barrels (2022) to 21% (2026; KSE label 42% of shadow in Aug 2026). Mainly Kozmino-China ESPO runs for private Chinese owners (Sunne, Prominent, Searun, Shang, Sino) plus serial single-ship companies; 80% treated as Chinese-controlled. Short-haul Kozmino trips earn about 0.6x the average crude freight per barrel. Plus IG-insured Chinese owners and COSCO's half of Arc7 LNG carriers (LNG part unchanged from shipping.json).

GRC.reasoning: Mainstream (G7+-linked, price-cap) fleet only. Greek beneficial owners' share of Russian seaborne barrels: crude 31% pre-war (Lloyd's List: a third of oil shipments Aug 2021), 40% in 2022 (LL: 50% of oil shipments Aug 2022, 42% of crude Oct 2022), 28% in 2023 (S&P: G7 tankers 52% of crude May 2023, Greeks 20%+ by Dec 2023), 13% in 2024 (S&P: Greek operators 11.5m bbl Jan, 16.6m bbl Feb 2024), 22% in 2025 (Kpler Jan-Jul 33% of crude; Windward 27% Jun, 16% Aug, <5% Nov after the EU cap cut), 9% in Jan-Aug 2026 (KSE top-10: Dynacom 3-6% of crude May-Aug, 2-5 Greek firms in the top 10). Products 28-38% throughout (Kpler 51% of fuel oil; Windward 43% of clean products Jun 2025; KSE: Greek firms hold 6-9 of the top-10 product shipper spots 2024-26). Cross-check: FT found USD 3.8bn for 389m priced barrels of crude Jul 2023-mid 2026 (scaled ~USD 1.8bn/yr); this model gives ~USD 1.65bn/yr for the same window. Greek-sold tankers now in the shadow fleet are NOT counted here (they are in shipping.json ship_sales).

HKG.reasoning: 45% of KSE 'China' managers assumed Hong Kong-registered (Glory Shipping HK, Eurus HKG etc.); 65% treated as foreign, since Sovcomflot-chain tankers also use Hong Kong shells (Comitana, Insania, Vimena, Anchorstar). Plus 21% of the opaque remainder.

overlaps: This file is a re-allocation of the freight part of shipping.json, not a new flow: use it INSTEAD of shipping.json freight (and instead of refine.json shipping_control scaling and the 2026 x1.065 factor), never in addition. Totals are close: all-foreign gross freight 2022-26 here vs shipping.json are given in totals; the difference is mostly the 2026 crude pool (11.0 vs 9.7 USD bn) and a larger Russian pool than shipping.json had before refine. Ship sales (Greek and other tankers sold into the shadow fleet) stay in shipping.json ship_sales and are not in these shares, so a Greek-built/ex-Greek tanker now run by a UAE front counts here for the controller (often Russia) and its sale premium counts for the seller in ship_sales - no double count. Services overlap (uncovered.json sold_to_rus) and CIF overlap with fossil-fuel payments are unchanged and handled by shipping.json overlap_share_with_services_sold_to_rus, which still applies per country. uncovered.json GRC.oil_shipping_earned remains replaced by shipping.json. Insurance by insurer country (UK, Norway IG clubs vs Ingosstrakh) is not re-estimated here.
notes: Gross freight, not profit. The biggest open guesses: the Russian-controlled share of opaque Seychelles/Marshall Islands/unknown-managed tankers (50%, range 25-80%), the mainland/Hong Kong split of KSE 'China' managers (55/45), and the non-Greek mainstream split. Greek 2026 products share (27%) is higher than shipping.json's 10% because KSE shows Greek firms holding 7-9 of the top-10 product shipper spots in Mar-Jun 2026.
